documents.title: After-hours call: lip swelling
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Sonia called this evening. Swelling started in her lips yesterday and now both eyelids and her hands are puffy too. No hives, no itch. Voice normal, swallowing ok, no breathing trouble right now. Some vague belly ache. Took her danazol as usual.
Given last year's laryngeal attack and intubation, told her to go to the ED now rather than wait it out at home, and to call 911 if her voice changes or she gets throat tightness on the way. Reminded her to tell triage it is hereditary angioedema, not an allergy - epinephrine/antihistamines don't help, C1 inhibitor does. She will go tonight with her father.

events.reason: Facial and extremity swelling, hereditary angioedema

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 03/10/2025 00:40. Observation discharge 03/11/2025 10:30.

HPI: 25-year-old with known hereditary angioedema type I on danazol, SLE with class IV nephritis in remission, and cold AIHA. Two days of steadily increasing swelling, first the lips, then the eyelids, hands and feet. No hives or pruritus. Says she has had attacks like this on and off for about five years, most fading without treatment, and one a year ago that closed her airway and needed intubation. Mild crampy belly discomfort. No new medications, no estrogen, no ACE inhibitor.
Meds: danazol 200 tid, mycophenolate 1000 bid, hydroxychloroquine 200 bid, prednisone 5, folic acid, vitamin D3. NKDA.

Exam: Vitals stable throughout. Marked non-pitting edema of both lips and both upper and lower eyelids, no redness or warmth. Uvula and tongue normal, voice normal, no stridor. Dorsal hand swelling. Abdomen: mild diffuse tenderness, no rebound, no guarding. Skin: no urticaria.

Labs: CBC normal. BMP normal. C4 5 mg/dL (low). Total IgE 38 IU/mL (normal). C1 inhibitor level sent - pending at discharge.

ED course: HAE attack, not allergic angioedema - no epinephrine or antihistamines. Plasma-derived C1 esterase inhibitor 20 units/kg IV at 01:30. Kept overnight in observation with airway equipment at bedside; ENT aware. Swelling clearly regressing by morning, abdominal discomfort gone, airway never involved.

Disposition: home 03/11. Continue home medications. Follow up with PCP this week and with allergy/immunology; C1 inhibitor result will go to allergy.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Going away for work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! I got a spot doing vet tech work at a big cattle ranch outside Flagstaff starting Feb 16, probably 6-8 weeks. Can I get 90 days of all my meds before I go? Also anything I should know being that far from my doctors?

documents.title: RE: Going away for work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That sounds like a great opportunity. I'll ask your specialists and the pharmacy for 90-day fills. Things to keep in mind: carry a list of your diagnoses and medicines (I'll put an updated summary in the portal), and the allergy letter about HAE treatment - any swelling in your face or throat means an ER, and tell them it's hereditary angioedema. Keep warm on cold mornings for your blood. If you get a fever while you're on mycophenolate and prednisone, get seen promptly - don't wait it out. Text me anytime.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Discharge Summary
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER, FLAGSTAFF AREA - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 03/05/2026 16:20. Discharged 03/11/2026. Service: Infectious Disease.

Principal diagnosis: Bubonic plague (Yersinia pestis), left inguinal bubo, with lung involvement.
Other: leukocytosis; thrombocytopenia; SLE with class IV lupus nephritis in remission; hereditary angioedema type I; cold autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

HPI: 26-year-old woman from Massachusetts working several weeks as a veterinary technician on a cattle ranch here, handling livestock and the ranch's stray cats. Four days of worsening fatigue and chills, a dry cough that turned blood-streaked, and pain in the left groin. A painful sore came up on her ankle shortly after she found and pulled a flea off her sock. Prior hospital care: kidney admission in 2024 and an angioedema ED stay with overnight observation in 2025.
Home meds: mycophenolate 1000 mg bid, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg bid, prednisone 5 mg daily, danazol 200 mg tid, folic acid 1 mg, vitamin D3 2000 IU. NKDA.

Arrival: T 39.2 C (102.6 F), HR 110, RR 30, BP 92/58, SpO2 91% on room air. Ill-appearing and short of breath. 1.5 cm necrotic ulcer on the lateral left ankle; several red macules over both lower legs; tender, fluctuant 4 cm mass in the left inguinal region; crackles at both lung bases.
Labs: WBC 21.4, platelets 92, hemoglobin 11.0, creatinine normal. Portable chest film with bilateral patchy airspace opacities.
Needle aspiration of the inguinal mass: purulent material, Gram stain showing abundant neutrophils with scattered gram-negative rods; culture grew Yersinia pestis, confirmed by the state public health laboratory 3/8.

Course: Droplet precautions for the first 48 hours of therapy. IV ciprofloxacin plus IV doxycycline from the night of admission; IV fluids (warmed, given her cold AIHA) and supplemental oxygen 2 L by nasal cannula; hydrocortisone stress dosing while hypotensive, back to prednisone 5 mg on day 3. Mycophenolate held. Defervesced by day 3, off oxygen day 4, node softening and less tender. Doxycycline stopped and ciprofloxacin changed to oral on day 5. The county health department and state public health were notified on admission and handled contact tracing. No angioedema or hemolysis during the stay.

Discharge medications:
- Ciprofloxacin 750 mg PO twice daily through 3/18/2026 (14 days total) - NEW
- Mycophenolate - HOLD until reviewed by ID at follow-up
- Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg bid, prednisone 5 mg daily, danazol 200 mg tid, folic acid 1 mg, vitamin D3 2000 IU - continue

Follow-up: ID telehealth 3/19; PCP in Massachusetts within a week of return; chest x-ray in 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: In the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I'm in the hospital in Flagstaff - they think it's plague from a flea, which I know sounds crazy. They started IV antibiotics last night and stopped my mycophenolate. Feeling a little less awful today. Just wanted you to know. They have my list.

documents.title: RE: In the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for letting me know - I'm glad you got care quickly. Please have the team fax the discharge summary to us, and let's see you as soon as you're home. Remind them about warmed fluids and that any swelling is HAE. Thinking of you.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM. Admitted 3/5-3/11 near Flagstaff with culture-proven bubonic plague (left inguinal bubo, lung involvement, hypotension at arrival) after a flea bite at the ranch where she was working. IV cipro + doxy, then oral cipro to finish 3/18. MMF held. Discharge summary received 3/13 and reviewed; phone contact 3/12. Flew home 3/14 with her father.

Now: no fever since day 3. Cough gone. Groin much better. Ankle sore scabbing over. Tired. Taking cipro bid, last dose tomorrow. Still holding MMF; ID telehealth 3/19 to decide restart.
Meds reconciled: ciprofloxacin 750 bid (through 3/18), HCQ 200 bid, prednisone 5, danazol 200 tid, folic acid, D3; MMF on hold.

Exam: Afebrile, vitals normal, SpO2 normal on RA. Weight 73 kg (77 in August). Lungs clear. Left inguinal node about 2 cm, soft, non-tender, no fluctuance or drainage. Lateral left ankle: 1 cm dry eschar, healing edges, no surrounding redness. Lower leg macules faded. No swelling.

Labs today: WBC 5.6, platelets 238, Hgb 11.5, CMP normal - leukocytosis and thrombocytopenia resolved.

A/P:
1. Bubonic plague - responding well; finish ciprofloxacin. ID will address MMF restart. Follow-up CXR late April.
2. Immunosuppression - MMF on hold; watch for lupus activity off it; nephrology and rheum updated.
3. Cipro with prednisone - stop and call if heel/Achilles pain.
4. Return precautions: fever, groin swelling, cough, shortness of breath.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (1000 mg) by mouth twice daily

INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC - TELEHEALTH 3/19/2026
Patient at home in Massachusetts.

Completed 14 days of therapy for Yersinia pestis bubonic plague yesterday. Afebrile for over two weeks, no cough or dyspnea, groin node shrinking and nearly painless, ankle lesion healed over per patient and her PCP's note of 3/17. Labs 3/17 normal.

Assessment: bubonic plague, clinically cured.
Plan: restart mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice daily today - discussed with her nephrologist. Follow-up chest x-ray in 6 weeks via PCP; no further ID follow-up needed unless symptoms recur.
